1. PurposeÂ 
The Department of Veterans Affairs is conducting market research to identify qualified businesses capable of providing professional tree removal services at the Martinsburg VA Medical Center. The Government seeks information regarding industry capability, business size and socioeconomic status, relevant experience, and anticipated availability. The information received may be used to support acquisition strategy and determine whether a future requirement may be suitable for a small business set-aside or another procurement approach.Â 
2. Requirement OverviewÂ 
The anticipated requirement is for a contractor to furnish all labor, supervision, materials, tools, equipment, transportation, traffic and pedestrian controls, and services necessary to remove six designated declining oak trees near the front entrance of the medical center campus.Â 
Remove six VA-designated declining oak trees using professional tree-removal and rigging methods.Â 
Cut each stump as close to grade as safely and reasonably practicable, not to exceed approximately six inches above surrounding grade unless otherwise directed. Stump grinding and stump/FboNotice removal are excluded.Â 
Remove all branches, logs, leaves, chips, and other debris from VA property and lawfully dispose of the material off site.Â 
Protect buildings, sidewalks, roadways, curbs, landscaping, utilities, signs, vehicles, and other Government property.Â 
Maintain safe medical center access and coordinate any temporary restrictions or closures with the VA point of contact.Â 
Establish appropriate work zones, exclusion zones, warning devices, barricades, spotters, and pedestrian/vehicle controls.Â 
Perform the work in accordance with applicable OSHA requirements and applicable ANSI Z133 and ANSI A300 standards.Â 
Coordinate scheduling and approved work hours to minimize disruption to medical center operations.Â 
3. Contractor QualificationsÂ 
Professional tree-care operations performed under the direction of qualified personnel, with a certified arborist and/or appropriately licensed tree expert available as applicable.Â 
All licenses, permits, certifications, insurance, and workers compensation coverage required by Federal, State, and local law maintained throughout performance.Â 
Ability to provide documentation of applicable certifications and insurance upon request.Â 
Capability to safely perform work in an active medical center environment while protecting patients, visitors, staff, vehicles, and property.Â
